column1: # libaom CfL (chroma-from-luma) ablation on the PHOTO gap — after palette/CDEF/restoration
# ruled out (see rd_gap_{palette,tool}_ablation_2026-07-01.tsv), tests whether CfL entirely
# on-vs-off brackets a meaningful share of the ~8-18% photo gap in docs/RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md.
# This is an UPPER BOUND on what a search-depth difference could matter: zenrav1e already
# implements CfL (rdo_cfl_alpha, src/rdo.rs:1786) with a bounded/adaptive alpha search, not
# "no CfL" — so the true zenrav1e-vs-libaom CfL delta is some fraction of this number, not
# all of it. Same corpus/settings as the other 2026-07-01 ablations, format 420, cpu-used=2,
# 22/22 images. Harness: scripts/rd_gap/tool_ablation.sh (VARIANTS="baseline=
# nocfl=--enable-cfl-intra=0"), zenavif dc22ee15adcc. libaom: git 632172a4 (aomenc 3.14.1).
# Scorer: fast-ssim2-cli v0.6.0.
# + = disabling CfL costs MORE bits (i.e. CfL was helping libaom).
# PHOTOS ONLY (families 1,2,3,5,6,8,9), matched-ssim2 frontier comparison:
variant
nocfl
nocfl
nocfl
nocfl
# -> Real, consistent-sign signal (unlike CDEF/restoration's noise) but small: CfL's total
#    value to libaom on this photo corpus is ~1.2-2.8% (median 1.2-1.7%). Since zenrav1e already
#    has a working (if bounded/adaptive, not exhaustive) CfL alpha search, the RECOVERABLE
#    fraction from tightening it is <= this number, likely well under it. Upper-bounds CfL's
#    contribution to the ~8-18% photo gap at roughly 1-2 percentage points -- real, but not the
#    dominant driver. Majority of the photo gap (~6-16 points) remains unexplained by any single
#    tool tested (palette, CDEF, restoration, tx-type, now CfL). See RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md.
